work.title: Rückert-Lieder
work.movement: Ich bin der Welt abhanden gekommen — concert-band arrangement

version.value: Arrangement for soprano, English horn solo and concert band; arranger not identified
version.note: Commons names the Navy Concert Band, a soprano and an English horn but does not name an arranger or edition. Mahler wrote the song for voice with piano or orchestra, so a band performance implies an arrangement. This recording’s chroma estimates read F major, whereas the first-edition orchestral score on IMSLP (22552) is notated in E♭ major; IMSLP lists the song in F major and notes transposed publications. The estimates suggest a possible pitch difference from that edition, but neither the arrangement’s key nor any transposition has been confirmed.

composition.value: Public domain: Mahler died in 1911 and the poet Friedrich Rückert in 1866.
composition.note: Commons applies PD/1923 tags to both the composition (author died 1911) and the lyrics (author died 1866). These cover the song and poem, not the unidentified band arrangement.

recording.value: Public domain in the United States as a work of a U.S. Navy sailor or employee made as part of official duties (Commons template PD-USGov-Navy); the file also carries the Public Domain Mark.
recording.note: This is a status under United States law for works of the federal government, as stated on Commons. The copyright status of the band arrangement itself is not addressed by the Commons tags and the arranger is unidentified.

sources.title: IMSLP: Rückert Lieder, GMW 39-43 (Mahler, Gustav)
sources.locator: Work page: catalogue numbers (GMW 41 for this song), first performance 29 January 1905 with Friedrich Weidemann, and the scores listed. The orchestral score used for structure is IMSLP22552 (first edition, E♭ major), whose song occupies PDF pp. 13–23.

sources.title: Universal Edition: Mahler, Ich bin der Welt abhanden gekommen — from “Rückert-Lieder” (1901) for voice and orchestra
sources.locator: Essay by Reinhold Kubik (autumn 2008): first draft dated 16 August 1901, the premiere of 29 January 1905 in the Brahms-Saal, Mahler’s remark about small halls, and the relation to the Fifth Symphony’s Adagietto.
